captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/18_sela, specifically its ResNet path (models/resnet_sela.py, utils/sinkhorn.py, data/sela_dataset.py, train_pretrain_resnet.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Asano et al. (2020) SeLa, torch/torchvision only (the Sinkhorn-Knopp optimal transport is pure torch). So it ports self-contained (no third_party submodule). The port keeps the capture directory numbering (18) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (this list's number 19 is SeLa -- see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Self-labelling via simultaneous clustering and representation learning

scope: The ResNet path is ported: a ResNet backbone (the official ResNetV2-50 by default, or a torchvision ResNet-50) with num_heads linear prototype heads (top_layer). Labels start from a balanced shuffled equipartition and are recomputed with Sinkhorn-Knopp optimal transport (which enforces an equipartitioned assignment over K clusters) at the official nopts scheduled points inside the batch loop; the network is trained with cross-entropy on the hard targets, averaged over the heads. Unlike DeepCluster the heads are never reset and there is no Sobel front-end. The capture's unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (models/vit_sela.py, arch: vit) is also ported additively: the same ViT-B/16 backbone every method shares with a single linear prototype head, self-labelled by per-epoch Sinkhorn-Knopp OT and trained with cross-entropy, AdamW + warmup/cosine + AMP, milestone checkpoints; the native ResNet path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
encoder: encoder.pt is the ResNet backbone (backbone.*): the feature trunk up to and including the final avg-pool, producing a 2048-d feature. The linear prototype heads (top_layer.*) are training machinery and are excluded -- the standard SSL convention of probing the backbone, the same shape as the deepcluster port (backbone kept, cluster heads excluded).
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the backbone's 2048-d feature via get_features(), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation -- the same normalisation SeLa trains with). Follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: the ResNet path and the unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (arch: vit) are both ported; the ViT path (models/vit_sela.py, train_pretrain_vit_sela.py, configs/pretrain_vit.yaml) is port-authored from the capture's train_step2_vit.py + models/vit_sela.py, is single-prototype-head (vs the native multi-head), reuses compute_hard_sinkhorn_assignments + create_indexed_train_loader, and adds timm as a lazy dependency
the Sinkhorn-Knopp internal iteration is kept in float64 (the official code raises softmax to a large power lambda that underflows float32), matching the capture

the official nopts label-optimisation schedule (build_optimize_times + in-loop pop) and the balanced-label initialisation are kept faithfully; the assignment is computed over the augmented train loader as in the official code
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture branched on torch.cuda / DataParallel)
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count; the checkpoint key state_dict is renamed model_state_dict to match this repo's port convention
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)

the training loop drops the upstream DataParallel/DistributedDataParallel, AMP autocast and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32; the SGD step-LR schedule is kept
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
